## FIELD/GREENHOUSE/LABORATORY EXPERIENCE

- Production of high-quality inoculum for disease assays
- Disease assays and phenotyping for disease and agronomic traits in field corn, sweet corn, soybean, and snap bean, in field and greenhouse settings
- Standardization of disease assay protocols
- Crop breeding efforts (soybean, maize, hemp, spinach, cowpea, common bean, arugula) in greenhouse and field
- Phenotypic data collection and analysis
- Genetic analysis (marker-trait association, QTL mapping, genomic prediction)
- Report writing on funded projects

## SELECTED PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE

- Designed and implemented a full multi-breed genomic prediction pipeline (univariate, bivariate, and multi-trait single-step GBLUP and GBLUP) for puberty and fertility traits across five beef cattle breed populations (Angus, Red Angus, Hereford, Bos indicus-influenced, and a pooled MultiBreed population of over 9,000 animals genotyped on an 800K SNP panel) using BLUPF90+/GIBBSF90+
- Conducted variance component estimation, heritability, and genetic correlation analysis via REML/AI-REML, and validated genomic prediction accuracy using the LR (Legarra & Reverter, 2018) temporal validation framework
- Extended weighted genomic prediction methodology to disease-resistance and abiotic-stress trait prediction in cowpea and common bean, using SNP weighting informed by meta-transcriptomic (RNA-seq) evidence
- Presented genomic prediction research at the Advances in Genome Biology and Technology (AGBT) Agricultural Meeting, 2025
- Involved in the design and implementation of experiments for disease and agronomic trait evaluation on vegetable crops (spinach, arugula, common bean) at the University of Arkansas, Fayetteville
- Prepared and communicated reports to stakeholders and the academic community, including conference/meeting attendance and co-authoring peer-reviewed research articles
- Involved in the planning and implementation of pathology research trials on field corn within Trait Assessment, North America, Syngenta Seeds Inc.
- Contributed to disease trait evaluation efforts on field corn, sweet corn, soybean, and snap bean for product advancement within Syngenta Seeds Inc.
- Prepared and communicated summaries/reports to stakeholders within Syngenta Seeds Inc.
- Handled the adoption of a proprietary data collection tool for field corn pathology trials within Trait Assessment, North America, Syngenta
- Served as a member of Market Segment Teams for Field Corn pathology traits in North America, Syngenta
- Provided support/technical expertise for various functions/teams on disease trait efforts within Syngenta
- Trained new hires and supervised seasonal technical personnel and a research associate within the Field Corn Pathology team, Trait Assessment, North America, Syngenta Seeds Inc.
- Developed biocontrol management strategies for black Sigatoka disease of banana at the International Institute of Tropical Agriculture (IITA-CGIAR), Ibadan, Nigeria
- Characterized the biology of plant pathogens causing diseases of economic importance in field corn and banana at IITA-CGIAR
- Participated in molecular marker evaluation of indigenous tomato genotypes for Fusarium wilt resistance as an undergraduate research assistant, Federal University of Agriculture, Abeokuta, Nigeria

## DATA/GENOMIC/STATISTICAL ANALYTICAL PROFICIENCY

**Quantitative genetics / genomic prediction:** Single-step GBLUP (ssGBLUP) and GBLUP via BLUPF90+/GIBBSF90+, including threshold models for binary traits; univariate, bivariate, and multi-trait mixed-model analyses; REML/AI-REML variance component estimation; heritability and genetic correlation estimation across multiple breed populations; genomic relationship matrix construction (VanRaden method)

**Validation methodology:** LR (Legarra & Reverter, 2018) temporal and cross-validation frameworks for genomic prediction accuracy, bias, and dispersion

**Weighted/informed genomic prediction:** SNP-weighting schemes informed by meta-transcriptomic (RNA-seq) evidence, applied to disease-resistance and abiotic-stress trait prediction in legume crops (cowpea, common bean)

**Population genetics:** Principal component analysis and population stratification correction (PLINK); genotype imputation (Beagle); variant filtering and manipulation (bcftools)

**Programming/computation:** R (sommer, lme4/lmerTest, tidyverse, ggplot2), Python, Perl, SQL, SAS, JMP, Quarto/R Markdown for reproducible reporting, shell scripting, HPC job orchestration (SLURM)

**Genomic/bioinformatics tools:** BLUPF90+/GIBBSF90+ family, PLINK, bcftools, Beagle, TASSEL, MEGA, QTL mapping and GWAS software, genomic selection models implemented in R

**Experience working with large-scale sequence and genotype data**, including 800K-SNP genotype panels and multi-breed populations exceeding 9,000 animals
